data.narrative:
Cerebras is a publicly listed semiconductor company founded by Andrew Feldman and four co-founders. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 public-stage companies in Chips & Semiconductors, supplemented by 8 private frontier-tech comparables including SambaNova Systems and PsiQuantum.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach. Across three same-sector, same-stage peers—Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B)—the median valuation is $2.3B. This wide range ($1.1B to $35.8B) reflects heterogeneity in market positioning and maturity within public semiconductors. Public-comp anchoring via price-to-sales multiples (median 21.5x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, a limitation common to private-company analysis.

The triangulated range is $1.9B to $2.6B, with a median of $2.3B derived from the single applicable method. This estimate is constrained by reliance on one valuation approach and the large dispersion in peer multiples, particularly the $35.8B outlier. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue disclosure needed for multiple-based methods and the structural differences between frontier-chip developers and legacy semiconductor players in the comp universe. The current public valuation of $39.2B sits materially above this range, suggesting either market pricing divergence or data gaps in the peer set.
